1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned LAC no. 243/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW))
Ram Dutta & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 2 of 11 aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.

entities.text: Ram Dutta & Ors. Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2636 Bigha 18 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28199 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2636 Bigha 18 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2636 Bighas 18 Biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/
per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.
LAC no. 243/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Dutta & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 3 of 11 4.

It is stated that the Award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and,
therefore, this reference has been filed with a view to reassess the market value of the land which has been wrongly assessed by the LAC.

6. Following are the grounds under which the reference petition has been filed :
i) The LAC has not considered that the said land is very fertile and fit for all commercial, residential, industrial, etc purposes and the said land is levelled more than 2 feet height from the nearby land.
The said land bears no defects but the LAC has assessed the market value at very low rate.
ii) The revenue estate of Village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari) is situated near the National Highway No. 10, Delhi Rohtak Road (Nangloi).

The said estate is surrounded by many prestigious colonies/village/ Industries area, etc and the value of each every commodity LAC no. 243/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW))
Ram Dutta & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 4 of 11 has been raised day by day, the value of which has also been increased day by day.
iii) The said Land has got potential value as many purposes and the same has been surrounded by Villages Mundka, Ghevra, Kanjhawala, Nangloi, Karala, Kirari,
Nithari, etc and it the market value is not less than Rs. 5,000/ per sq. yards.
iv) The land of the petitioners is adjacent to welldeveloped areas, colonies and hence has a great market value.

sentences.text: The land enjoys all type of modern facilities/ amenities like developed telephone, electricity, water connection, public school, Govt. School and most frequently severed by DTC, Railway Station and other transportation.

v) The LAC has not legally assessed the market value of the land rather he has wholly and solely relied on the policy announcement and which come into effect from the financial year 20012002 in which the Government fixed the indicative prices of agricultural land at the rate of Rs.
15.70 lacs per acre for the acquisition of the Agricultural land.
The LAC has further not made any efforts to find out the market value of the land in the village.

vi) The land of the petitioners is surrounded by DDA PhaseII, DSIDC Project Bawana, PVC market Tikri Kalan, Indene bottling Plant Ghevra, Nangloi, Mundka Railway Station, Metro Project Mundka, National Highway No. 10, Village Pooth Kalan, Budh Vihar, Rama Vihar, Rithala, Karala just near the famous colonies Prem Nagar, Agar Nagar, Rani Khera and Colony, Madanpur Dabas,

3 sq. yards.
vii)

The petitioner's land is situated just near 100 mtr. Road which is connected to Sector 30, 31,
32, 21, 22, 28 and 29 (connected National Highway No. 1 to 10) and Chhotu Ram Institute of Technology, Netaji Subhash Tourist Complex, and famous prestigious school Ganga International Maharaja Agarsen Institution
are a stone throw from the land of the claimant.

Land of the claimant is quite adjacent to the Abadi area of Village Mundka, Ghevra, and Kirari Suleman Nagar, nangloi and there are thousands of industries working in the above said surrounding area, thus, the market value of land of the petitioner is very high.

7. It is stated that in view of these facts and circumstances and keeping in view the consideration of the petitioners, petitioners are claiming compensation for their acquired land at Rs. 5,000/ per sq.
yards.
The petitioners have claimed a solatium @ 30% on the market value and additional amount.
Interest at the amount due to the petitioners in accordance with the law and all other statutory benefits with damages of the crops @ Rs. 1,00,000/ per acre.

8. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/ Land Acquisition Collector (North West) and, it is, inter alia, submitted that the notification under Section 4 was passed on 21.03.2003 and the declaration LAC no. 243/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Dutta & Ors. Vs.
Union of India Page no. 6 of 11 under Section 6 of the Act was issued on 01.03.2003 and the said land has been acquired for the public purposes i.e. for Planned Development of Delhi.

sentences.text: It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.
12. It is stated that the possession of the said land has been taken over by the LAC/ L&B department on 13.10.2006 and after taking possession, the same was transferred to DDA on the same day.

All the other averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition were denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action, therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is level to be dismissed with cost.
13. On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 10.02.2015:  ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent?
OPP 2. Relief.

sentences.text: Matter was listed for recording of petitioners evidence.

Ld. Counsel for the petitioner as well as Ld. Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 459 of 2016, Ajit Singh Vs. Union of India.

entities.text: Ajit Singh Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
15. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under : 
1.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent?
OPP 16.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
17. To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Ajit Singh (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 18.10.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.

sentences.text: Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

19. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari) is covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

20. In the case of Ajit Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 25 of 200506 dated 06.02.2006 as Rs.
19,45,800/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Ajit Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Ajit Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
21. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF LAC no. 243/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Dutta & Ors.
Vs. Union of India Page no. 10 of 11 22.

As per the reference petition forwarded by LAC, the possession of land bearing Khasra No.
10/15/1, 16/2 and 4/14 (001) has not been taken which has been admitted by the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner is not entitled for enhancement of compensation qua this land.
23. In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioner @ Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(2) Additional amount @ 12% (
in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).

(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
24.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
